title_en: Legislation Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated in accordance with the Constitution with a view to regulating legislative activities, improving the national legislative system, enhancing legislative quality, perfecting the socialist legal system with Chinese characteristics, giving play to the guiding and driving role of legislation, ensuring and developing socialist democracy, comprehensively advancing the rule of law, and building a socialist country under the rule of law.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to the enactment, revision and abolition of laws, administrative regulations, local regulations, autonomous regulations and separate regulations.
The enactment, revision and abolition of rules of the departments of the State Council and local government rules shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law.

Article 3 Legislation shall adhere to the leadership of the Communist Party of China, be guided by Marxism-Leninism, Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the important thought of Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, promote the construction of the rule of law system under socialism with Chinese characteristics, and ensure the comprehensive construction of a modern socialist country on the track of the rule of law.

Article 4 Legislation shall adhere to taking economic construction as the center, adhere to reform and opening up, implement the new development concept, and ensure the comprehensive advancement of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation with Chinese-style modernization.

Article 5 Legislation shall conform to the provisions, principles and spirit of the Constitution, in accordance with the statutory authority and procedures, proceed from the overall interests of the State, and safeguard the unity, dignity and authority of the socialist legal system.

Article 6 Legislation shall adhere to and develop whole-process people's democracy, respect and protect human rights, and safeguard and promote social fairness and justice.
Legislation shall reflect the will of the people, promote socialist democracy, adhere to the openness of legislation, and ensure that the people participate in legislative activities through various channels.

Article 7 Legislation shall proceed from reality, adapt to the requirements of economic and social development and comprehensive deepening of reform, and scientifically and reasonably stipulate the rights and obligations of citizens, legal persons and other organizations, and the powers and responsibilities of state organs.
Legal norms shall be clear, specific, targeted and enforceable.

Article 8 Legislation shall advocate and promote the core socialist values, adhere to the combination of rule of law and rule of virtue, strengthen the sense of community of the Chinese nation, and promote the construction of socialist spiritual civilization.

Article 9 Legislation shall adapt to the needs of reform, adhere to the unity of promoting reform under the rule of law and perfecting the rule of law in reform, guide, promote, regulate and guarantee relevant reforms, and give play to the important role of the rule of law in the modernization of the national governance system and governance capacity.

Article 10 The National People's Congress and the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall exercise the legislative power of the State in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
The National People's Congress shall enact and amend basic laws concerning criminal matters, civil matters, the structure of the State and other basic matters.
The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall enact and amend laws other than those that shall be enacted by the National People's Congress; during the recess of the National People's Congress, the Standing Committee may partially supplement and amend laws enacted by the National People's Congress, provided that such supplement and amendment shall not contravene the basic principles of such laws.
The National People's Congress may authorize the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress to enact relevant laws.

Article 12 If no law has yet been enacted on a matter provided for in Article 11 of this Law, the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall have the power to make a decision to authorize the State Council to formulate, according to actual needs, administrative regulations for part of such matters, except for matters concerning crimes and penalties, the deprivation of political rights of citizens, compulsory measures and penalties restricting personal freedom, and the judicial system.

Article 13 An authorization decision shall specify the purpose, matters, scope, duration, and the principles to be followed by the authorized organ in implementing the authorization decision.
The duration of an authorization shall not exceed five years, unless otherwise provided in the authorization decision.
The authorized organ shall, six months prior to the expiration of the authorization duration, report to the authorizing organ on the implementation of the authorization decision and submit its opinions on whether it is necessary to enact relevant laws; if continued authorization is needed, the authorized organ may submit relevant opinions, and the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall make a decision.

Article 14 Where the conditions for formulating a law on an authorized legislative matter have matured after practical testing, the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall promptly enact a law. After the enactment of such law, the authorization for the corresponding legislative matter shall terminate.

Article 15 The authorized organ shall exercise the conferred power strictly in accordance with the authorization decision.
The authorized organ shall not delegate the conferred power to any other organ.

Article 16 The National People's Congress and its Standing Committee may, in light of the needs of reform and development, decide to authorize, for a specified period and within a specified scope, the temporary adjustment or temporary suspension of application of some provisions of a law regarding specific matters.
Where matters for which the temporary adjustment or temporary suspension of application of some provisions of a law is authorized prove to be feasible in practice, the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall promptly amend the relevant law; where the conditions for amending the law are not yet mature, the authorization period may be extended, or the implementation of relevant legal provisions may be resumed.

Article 17 The Presidium of the National People's Congress may submit a legislative bill to the National People's Congress, and the bill shall be deliberated by the session of the National People's Congress.
The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the State Council, the Central Military Commission, the National Commission of Supervision, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the special committees of the National People's Congress may submit legislative bills to the National People's Congress, and the Presidium shall decide whether to place them on the agenda of the session.

Article 18 A delegation or a group of thirty or more deputies may submit a legislative bill to the National People's Congress, and the Presidium shall decide whether to place it on the agenda of the session, or may first refer it to the relevant special committee for deliberation, which shall submit its opinion on whether to place it on the agenda, and then decide whether to place it on the agenda.
When the special committee deliberates, it may invite the proposer to attend the meeting as a nonvoting participant and express opinions.

Article 19 A legislative bill to be submitted to the National People's Congress may, during the recess of the National People's Congress, be first submitted to the Standing Committee. After deliberation at a meeting of the Standing Committee in accordance with the relevant procedures provided for in Section 3 of Chapter II of this Law, the Standing Committee shall decide to submit the bill to the National People's Congress for deliberation, and the Standing Committee or the proposer shall make an explanation to the plenary session of the Congress.
When the Standing Committee deliberates a legislative bill in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, it shall solicit opinions from deputies to the National People's Congress through various means and provide feedback on the relevant circumstances; when the special committees and the working bodies of the Standing Committee conduct legislative research, they may invite relevant deputies to the National People's Congress to participate.

Article 20 Where the Standing Committee decides to submit a legislative bill to the National People's Congress for deliberation, it shall distribute the draft law to the deputies one month before the session is held, and may, at an appropriate time, organize the deputies to study and discuss the draft and solicit their opinions.

Article 21 Where a legislative bill is placed on the agenda of a session of the National People's Congress, after the plenary session of the Congress hears the explanation of the proposer, the various delegations shall deliberate the bill.
When the various delegations deliberate the legislative bill, the proposer shall send persons to listen to opinions and answer inquiries.
When the various delegations deliberate the legislative bill, upon request of a delegation, relevant organs and organizations shall send persons to explain relevant information.

Article 22 Where a legislative bill is placed on the agenda of a session of the National People's Congress, the relevant special committee shall deliberate the bill, submit its deliberation opinion to the Presidium, and distribute it to the session.

Article 23 Where a legislative bill is placed on the agenda of a session of the National People's Congress, the Constitution and Law Committee shall, based on the deliberation opinions of the various delegations and the relevant special committee, conduct a unified deliberation on the bill, submit a report on the deliberation result and a revised draft of the law to the Presidium, and shall, in the report on the deliberation result, explain the constitutional issues involved and significant differing opinions; after such report and draft are examined and adopted by a meeting of the Presidium, they shall be distributed to the session.

Article 24 Where a legislative bill is placed on the agenda of a session of the National People's Congress, if necessary, the executive chairpersons of the Presidium may convene a meeting of heads of delegations to hear the deliberation opinions of the various delegations on major issues in the bill, conduct discussions, and report the discussions and opinions to the Presidium.
The executive chairpersons of the Presidium may also convene relevant deputies elected by the delegations to discuss major specialized issues in the bill and report the discussions and opinions to the Presidium.

Article 25 Where a legislative bill placed on the agenda of a session of the National People's Congress is requested to be withdrawn by the proposer before being submitted for vote, the proposer shall state the reasons, and upon the consent of the Presidium and a report to the Congress, the deliberation of the legislative bill shall terminate.

Article 26 Where a legislative bill under deliberation has major issues that need further study, upon proposal by the Presidium and decision by the plenary session of the Congress, the Congress may authorize the Standing Committee to further deliberate based on the opinions of the deputies, make a decision, and report the decision to the next session of the National People's Congress; or may authorize the Standing Committee to further deliberate based on the opinions of the deputies, propose a revision plan, and submit it to the next session of the National People's Congress for deliberation and decision.

Article 27 After the revised draft of a law is deliberated by the various delegations, the Constitution and Law Committee shall modify it based on the deliberation opinions of the various delegations, and submit a final draft of the law for vote. The Presidium shall submit such final draft to the plenary session of the Congress for vote, and the draft shall be adopted by a majority vote of all deputies.
Article 28 A law adopted by the National People's Congress shall be promulgated by the President of the State by issuing a presidential decree.

Article 29 The Council of Chairpersons may submit a legislative bill to the Standing Committee, and the bill shall be deliberated at a meeting of the Standing Committee.
The State Council, the Central Military Commission, the National Commission of Supervision, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the special committees of the National People's Congress may submit legislative bills to the Standing Committee. The Council of Chairpersons shall decide whether to place them on the agenda of a meeting of the Standing Committee, or may first refer them to the relevant special committee for deliberation and report, and then decide whether to place them on the agenda. If the Council of Chairpersons considers that a legislative bill has major issues that need further study, it may suggest that the proposer revise and improve the bill before submitting it to the Standing Committee.

Article 30 If ten or more members of the Standing Committee jointly submit a bill to the Standing Committee, the Council of Chairpersons shall decide whether to place it on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting, or shall first refer it to the relevant special committee for deliberation and an opinion on whether to place it on the agenda, and then decide whether to place it on the agenda. If it is not placed on the agenda, it shall be reported to the meeting of the Standing Committee or explained to the proposer.
When the special committee deliberates the bill, it may invite the proposer to attend the meeting and express opinions.

Article 31 For a bill placed on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting, the draft law shall, unless under special circumstances, be distributed to the members of the Standing Committee seven days before the meeting is held.
When the Standing Committee meeting deliberates a bill, relevant deputies of the National People's Congress shall be invited to attend the meeting.

Article 32 A bill placed on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting shall, as a general rule, be deliberated at three Standing Committee meetings before being submitted for vote.
At the first meeting of the Standing Committee for deliberation, the proposer's explanation shall be heard at the plenary meeting, and preliminary deliberation shall be conducted by group meetings.
At the second meeting, a report on the revision of the draft law and major issues from the Constitution and Law Committee shall be heard at the plenary meeting, and further deliberation shall be conducted by group meetings.
At the third meeting, a report on the results of deliberation of the draft law from the Constitution and Law Committee shall be heard at the plenary meeting, and the revised draft law shall be deliberated by group meetings.
When the Standing Committee deliberates a bill, it may, as necessary, hold a joint group meeting or plenary meeting to discuss major issues in the draft law.

Article 33 A bill placed on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting, on which opinions from various sides are relatively consistent, may be submitted for vote after deliberation at two Standing Committee meetings; a bill involving relatively single items of adjustment or partial amendment, on which opinions from various sides are relatively consistent, or in case of urgency, may be submitted for vote after deliberation at only one Standing Committee meeting.

Article 34 When a group meeting of the Standing Committee deliberates a bill, the proposer shall send persons to listen to opinions and answer inquiries.
When a group meeting of the Standing Committee deliberates a bill, upon request of the group, relevant organs or organizations shall send persons to introduce the relevant information.

Article 35 A bill placed on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting shall be deliberated by the relevant special committee, which shall put forward its deliberation opinions and have them printed and distributed to the Standing Committee meeting.
When the relevant special committee deliberates a bill, it may invite members of other special committees to attend the meeting and express opinions.

Article 36 A bill placed on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting shall be uniformly deliberated by the Constitution and Law Committee based on the deliberation opinions of the members of the Standing Committee and the relevant special committee as well as opinions from various sides, and the Constitution and Law Committee shall submit a report on the revision or a report on the results of deliberation, and a revised draft law, and shall explain in the report on the revision or the report on the results of deliberation the constitutional issues involved and major dissenting opinions. If the deliberation opinions of the relevant special committee are not adopted, feedback shall be given to the relevant special committee.
When the Constitution and Law Committee deliberates a bill, members of the relevant special committees shall be invited to attend the meeting and express opinions.

Article 37 When a special committee deliberates a bill, it shall hold a plenary meeting for deliberation, and may, as necessary, request relevant organs or organizations to send relevant responsible persons to explain the relevant information.
Article 38 When special committees have inconsistent opinions on major issues of a draft law, they shall report to the Council of Chairpersons.

Article 39 For a bill placed on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting, the Constitution and Law Committee, the relevant special committee, and the working organs of the Standing Committee shall solicit opinions from various sides. Opinions may be solicited through seminars, appraisal meetings, hearings, and other forms.
If a bill involves highly professional issues requiring a feasibility evaluation, an appraisal meeting shall be held to hear opinions from relevant experts, departments, deputies of the National People's Congress, and other relevant parties. The appraisal shall be reported to the Standing Committee.
If a bill involves major differences in opinion or involves major adjustment of interests and a hearing is necessary, a hearing shall be held to hear opinions from relevant grassroots and group representatives, departments, people's organizations, experts, deputies of the National People's Congress, and other relevant social parties. The hearing shall be reported to the Standing Committee.
The working organs of the Standing Committee shall send the draft law to deputies of the National People's Congress in relevant fields, the standing committees of local people's congresses, as well as relevant departments, organizations, and experts for opinions.

Article 40 A bill placed on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting shall, after the Standing Committee meeting, be published to the public for comment, together with the draft law and explanation of its drafting and revision, unless the Council of Chairpersons decides not to publish it. The time for public comment shall generally be not less than thirty days. The status of comments received shall be reported to the public.

Article 41 For a bill placed on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting, the working organs of the Standing Committee shall collect and compile the opinions from group meetings, opinions from various sides, and other relevant materials, and distribute them to the Constitution and Law Committee and the relevant special committee, and, as necessary, print and distribute them to the Standing Committee meeting.

Article 42 For a bill to be submitted to the Standing Committee meeting for approval, before the Constitution and Law Committee submits a report on the results of deliberation, the working organs of the Standing Committee may evaluate the feasibility of the main institutional norms in the draft law, the timing of promulgation, the social effects of implementation, and potential issues. The evaluation results shall be explained by the Constitution and Law Committee in the report on the results of deliberation.

Article 43 Where a proposer requests to withdraw a bill placed on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting before it is submitted for vote, the proposer shall state the reasons, and upon approval by the Council of Chairpersons and a report to the Standing Committee, the deliberation of the bill shall be terminated.

Article 44 After the revised draft law is deliberated at the Standing Committee meeting, the Constitution and Law Committee shall revise it based on the deliberation opinions of the members of the Standing Committee, and submit a final draft for vote. The Council of Chairpersons shall request the plenary meeting of the Standing Committee to vote on it, and it shall be adopted by a majority vote of all members of the Standing Committee.
Before the final draft for vote is submitted for vote at the Standing Committee meeting, the Council of Chairpersons may, based on the circumstances of the deliberation, decide to submit individual important clauses with significant differences in opinion to the Standing Committee meeting for separate vote.
After the clause subject to separate vote is voted on at the Standing Committee meeting, the Council of Chairpersons may, based on the outcome of the separate vote, decide either to submit the final draft for vote, or to temporarily refrain from submitting for vote and refer it to the Constitution and Law Committee and the relevant special committee for further deliberation.

Article 45 Where a bill placed on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting is shelved for deliberation for two full years due to major differences in opinion among various sides on major issues such as the necessity and feasibility of formulating the law, or where the bill has not been placed on the agenda of the Standing Committee meeting for deliberation for two years after being temporarily not submitted for vote, the Council of Chairpersons may decide to terminate the deliberation and report to the Standing Committee; if necessary, the Council of Chairpersons may also decide to postpone the deliberation.

Article 46 Where revisions are made to individual provisions involving similar matters in multiple laws and a single bill is submitted therefor, upon decision by the Council of Chairpersons, the bill may be voted on jointly or separately.
Article 47 A law adopted by the Standing Committee shall be promulgated by the President through a presidential order.

Article 48 The power of interpretation of laws belongs to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.
The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall interpret a law under any of the following circumstances:
(1) If the specific meaning of a provision of the law needs to be further clarified;
(2) If new circumstances arise after the enactment of the law and the applicable legal basis needs to be clarified.

Article 49 The State Council, the Central Military Commission, the National Commission of Supervision, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the special committees of the National People's Congress may request the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress to interpret a law or may submit relevant bills.
The standing committees of the people's congresses of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may request the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress to interpret a law.

Article 50 The working bodies of the Standing Committee shall study and draft a legislative interpretation draft, and the Council of Chairmen shall decide to place it on the agenda of a meeting of the Standing Committee.

Article 51 After the legislative interpretation draft is deliberated at a meeting of the Standing Committee, the Constitution and Law Committee shall deliberate and revise it in accordance with the deliberation opinions of the members of the Standing Committee and submit a draft for vote on the legislative interpretation.

Article 52 The draft for vote on the legislative interpretation shall be adopted by a majority vote of all members of the Standing Committee, and shall be published by announcement issued by the Standing Committee.
Article 53 The legislative interpretations of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall have the same effect as laws.
Article 54 The National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall strengthen the organization and coordination of legislative work and play a leading role in legislative work.

Article 55 The National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall adhere to scientific legislation, democratic legislation, and legislation in accordance with law, and through various forms such as enacting, amending, abolishing, and interpreting laws and compiling codes, enhance the systematization, integration, coordination, and timeliness of legislation.

Article 56 The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall, through forms such as legislative plans, annual legislative plans, and special legislative plans, strengthen the overall arrangement of legislative work. When formulating legislative plans and legislative plans, it shall carefully study the proposals and suggestions of deputies, extensively solicit opinions, conduct scientific demonstration and evaluation, and determine legislative projects in accordance with the needs of economic and social development and the construction of democracy and the rule of law, and in accordance with the requirements of strengthening legislation in key areas, emerging areas, and foreign-related areas. The legislative plans and legislative plans shall be adopted by the Council of Chairmen and published to the public.
The working bodies of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall be responsible for formulating legislative plans and drafting legislative plans, and shall, in accordance with the requirements of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, supervise the implementation of the legislative plans and legislative plans.

Article 57 The relevant special committees of the National People's Congress and the working bodies of the Standing Committee shall participate in advance in the drafting of relevant legal drafts; for comprehensive, overall, and fundamental important legal drafts, the relevant special committees or the working bodies of the Standing Committee may organize the drafting.
For legal drafts with strong professionalism, experts in relevant fields may be invited to participate in the drafting work, or the drafting may be entrusted to relevant experts, teaching and research units, or social organizations.

Article 58 When a legislative bill is submitted, the text of the draft law and its explanation shall be submitted simultaneously, and necessary reference materials shall be provided. Where a law is to be amended, a comparative text before and after the amendment shall also be submitted. The explanation of the draft law shall include the necessity, feasibility, and main content of enacting or amending the law, relevant opinions concerning constitutionality issues, and the coordination and handling of major divergent opinions during the drafting process.
Article 59 A legislative bill submitted to the National People's Congress or its Standing Committee may be withdrawn by the proposer before it is placed on the agenda of a meeting.

Article 60 Where a legislative bill submitted to a plenary meeting of the National People's Congress or its Standing Committee for vote is not adopted, if the proposer considers that the law must be enacted, it may be resubmitted in accordance with the procedures prescribed by law, and the Presidium or the Council of Chairmen shall decide whether to place it on the agenda of a meeting; among them, a legislative bill that is not adopted by the National People's Congress shall be submitted to the National People's Congress for deliberation and decision.
Article 61 A law shall clearly specify the date of coming into force.

Article 62 The order of the President signed to promulgate a law shall state the enacting organ, the date of adoption, and the date of coming into force of the law.
After the law is signed and promulgated, the text of the law, the explanation of the draft law, the report on the deliberation results, etc., shall be promptly published in the Bulletin of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, on the website of the National People's Congress, and in newspapers distributed nationwide.
The text of the law published in the Bulletin of the Standing Committee shall be the standard text.

Article 63 The procedures for amendment and abolition of laws shall be governed by the relevant provisions of this Chapter.
Where a law is amended, a new text of the law shall be published.
Where a law is abolished, unless the abolition of the law is provided for by another law, it shall be published by an order of the President signed by the President.

Article 64 Where a draft law is inconsistent with the relevant provisions of other laws, the proposer shall explain the situation and propose handling opinions, and when necessary, shall simultaneously submit a proposal for amending or abolishing the relevant provisions of other laws.
When the Constitution and Law Committee or the relevant special committees deliberate a legislative bill, if they consider that the relevant provisions of other laws need to be amended or abolished, they shall propose handling opinions.

Article 65 A law may, as required by its content, be divided into parts, chapters, sections, articles, paragraphs, subparagraphs, and items.
The serial numbers of parts, chapters, sections, and articles shall be expressed in Chinese numerals sequentially; paragraphs shall not be numbered; the serial numbers of subparagraphs shall be expressed in Chinese numerals with brackets sequentially; the serial numbers of items shall be expressed in Arabic numerals sequentially.
The annotation of the title of a law shall state the enacting organ and the date of adoption. For a law that has been amended, the amending organ and the date of amendment shall be stated sequentially.
The working bodies of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall formulate technical specifications for legislation.

Article 66 Where a law explicitly requires the relevant state organs to formulate specific supporting provisions on a special matter, the relevant state organs shall formulate the provisions within one year from the date of coming into force of the law; if the law otherwise provides for the time limit for formulating the specific supporting provisions, that provision shall prevail. Where the relevant state organs fail to formulate the specific supporting provisions within the time limit, they shall explain the situation to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.

Article 67 The relevant special committees of the National People's Congress and the working bodies of the Standing Committee may organize post-legislative evaluation of relevant laws or relevant provisions in laws. The evaluation situation shall be reported to the Standing Committee.
Article 68 Where the National People's Congress or its Standing Committee makes decisions on legal issues, the relevant provisions of this Law shall apply.

Article 69 The working bodies of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may study and reply to inquiries on specific legal questions, and shall report them to the Standing Committee for recordation.

Article 70 The working organs of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall, based on actual needs, establish grassroots legislative contact points to deeply listen to the opinions of grassroots people and relevant parties on draft laws and legislative work.

Article 71 The working organs of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall strengthen legislative publicity work, releasing legislative information, introducing circumstances, and responding to concerns through various forms.

Article 72 The State Council shall formulate administrative regulations in accordance with the Constitution and laws.
Administrative regulations may provide for the following matters:
(1) matters requiring the formulation of administrative regulations for the implementation of the provisions of laws;
(2) matters concerning the administrative management functions of the State Council as stipulated in Article 89 of the Constitution.
For matters that shall be governed by laws enacted by the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee, if the State Council, with the authorization of the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee, first formulates administrative regulations, after practical testing and when the conditions for enacting laws are mature, the State Council shall promptly request the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee to enact laws.

Article 73 The legislative affairs institution of the State Council shall, in accordance with the overall work deployment of the State, draft the annual legislative plan of the State Council, and submit it to the State Council for approval. The legislative items in the annual legislative plan of the State Council shall be aligned with the legislative plan and legislative planning of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. The legislative affairs institution of the State Council shall timely track and understand the implementation of the legislative plan by the various departments of the State Council, and strengthen organization, coordination, supervision and guidance.
If a relevant department of the State Council deems it necessary to formulate administrative regulations, it shall submit an application for project establishment to the State Council.

Article 74 Administrative regulations shall be specifically drafted by the relevant departments of the State Council or the legislative affairs institution of the State Council. Drafts of laws and administrative regulations concerning important administration shall be organized for drafting by the legislative affairs institution of the State Council. In the process of drafting administrative regulations, opinions of relevant organs, organizations, deputies to the People's Congress, and the public shall be extensively solicited. Soliciting opinions may take various forms such as symposia, demonstration meetings, and hearings.
The draft of an administrative regulation shall be published to the public for comments, unless the State Council decides not to publish it.

Article 75 After the drafting of an administrative regulation is completed, the drafting unit shall submit the draft, its explanation, different opinions on the main issues of the draft from various parties, and other relevant materials to the legislative affairs institution of the State Council for review.
The legislative affairs institution of the State Council shall submit a review report and a revised draft to the State Council, and the review report shall explain the main issues of the draft.
Article 76 The decision procedure for administrative regulations shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Organic Law of the State Council of the People's Republic of China.

Article 77 Administrative regulations shall be promulgated by an order of the State Council signed by the Premier.
Administrative regulations concerning national defense construction may be promulgated by an order of the State Council and the Central Military Commission jointly signed by the Premier of the State Council and the Chairman of the Central Military Commission.

Article 78 After an administrative regulation is signed and promulgated, it shall be promptly published in the Bulletin of the State Council, on the China Legal Information Network of the Government, and in newspapers distributed nationwide.
The text of the administrative regulation published in the Bulletin of the State Council shall be the standard text.

Article 79 The State Council may, based on the needs of reform and development, decide to temporarily adjust or temporarily suspend the application of certain provisions of an administrative regulation within a specified period and scope for specific matters in administrative management and other fields.

Article 80 The People's Congress and its Standing Committee of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government may, in light of the specific conditions and actual needs of their respective administrative regions and provided that they do not contravene the Constitution, laws, and administrative regulations, formulate local regulations.

Article 81 The People's Congress and its Standing Committee of a city divided into districts may, in light of the specific conditions and actual needs of that city and provided that they do not contravene the Constitution, laws, administrative regulations, and the local regulations of the province or autonomous region, formulate local regulations on matters such as urban and rural development and management, ecological civilization construction, historical and cultural protection, and grassroots governance; where laws provide otherwise on matters for which a city divided into districts may formulate local regulations, such provisions shall prevail. Local regulations of a city divided into districts shall be submitted to the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the province or autonomous region for approval before they come into force. The Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the province or autonomous region shall examine the legality of the local regulations submitted for approval, and if it finds that they do not contravene the Constitution, laws, administrative regulations, and the local regulations of the province or autonomous region, it shall approve them within four months.
When examining the local regulations of a city divided into districts submitted for approval, if the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the province or autonomous region finds that such regulations contravene the rules of the people's government of the province or autonomous region, it shall make a decision on how to handle the matter.
Except for the city where the people's government of a province or autonomous region is located, the city where a special economic zone is located, and the larger city already approved by the State Council, the specific steps and timing for other cities divided into districts to begin formulating local regulations shall be determined by the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the province or autonomous region, taking into comprehensive consideration the population size, geographic area, economic and social development, as well as legislative needs and legislative capacity of the cities divided into districts under its jurisdiction, and shall be reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and the State Council for recordation.
The People's Congress and its Standing Committee of an autonomous prefecture may exercise the power of a city divided into districts to formulate local regulations in accordance with paragraph 1 of this Article. The specific steps and timing for an autonomous prefecture to begin formulating local regulations shall be determined in accordance with the preceding paragraph.
Local regulations that have already been formulated by the city where the people's government of a province or autonomous region is located, the city where a special economic zone is located, or the larger city already approved by the State Council, and which involve matters beyond the scope specified in paragraph 1 of this Article, shall remain in effect.

Article 82 Local regulations may provide for the following matters:
(1) Matters that require specific provisions in light of the actual conditions of the administrative region in order to implement the provisions of laws and administrative regulations;
(2) Matters that are local affairs and need to be regulated by local regulations.
Where the State has not yet enacted a law or administrative regulation on matters other than those specified in Article 11 of this Law, the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, as well as a city divided into districts or an autonomous prefecture, may first formulate local regulations based on the specific conditions and actual needs of the locality. After the law or administrative regulation enacted by the State takes effect, any provisions of the local regulations that contravene the law or administrative regulation shall be invalid, and the formulating organ shall promptly amend or abolish them.
The formulation of local regulations by a city divided into districts or an autonomous prefecture under paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article shall be limited to the matters specified in paragraph 1 of Article 81 of this Law.
When formulating local regulations, repetitive provisions on the content already clearly provided for in the superior law shall generally not be made.

Article 83 The People's Congress and its Standing Committee of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, and of a city divided into districts or an autonomous prefecture, may, in light of the needs for coordinated regional development, jointly formulate local regulations to be implemented in their respective administrative regions or in the relevant regions.
Provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, cities divided into districts, and autonomous prefectures may establish a working mechanism for regional coordinated legislation.

Article 84 The People's Congress and its Standing Committee of the province or city where a special economic zone is located may, in accordance with the authorization decision of the National People's Congress, formulate regulations to be implemented within the scope of the special economic zone.
The People's Congress and its Standing Committee of Shanghai Municipality may, in accordance with the authorization decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, formulate regulations for the Pudong New Area, to be implemented in the Pudong New Area.
The People's Congress and its Standing Committee of Hainan Province may, in accordance with legal provisions, formulate regulations for the Hainan Free Trade Port, to be implemented within the scope of the Hainan Free Trade Port.

Article 85 The People's Congress of a national autonomous area shall have the power, in accordance with the political, economic, and cultural characteristics of the local ethnic group(s), to formulate autonomous regulations and separate regulations. The autonomous regulations and separate regulations of an autonomous region shall be submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for approval before they take effect. The autonomous regulations and separate regulations of an autonomous prefecture or autonomous county shall be submitted to the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for approval before they take effect.
Autonomous regulations and separate regulations may, in accordance with the characteristics of the local ethnic group(s), make adaptive provisions regarding the provisions of laws and administrative regulations; however, they shall not contravene the basic principles of the laws or administrative regulations, nor shall they make adaptive provisions regarding the provisions of the Constitution and the Law on Regional Ethnic Autonomy, or other laws and administrative regulations that specifically provide for matters concerning national autonomous areas.
Article 86 Local regulations that provide for particularly important matters of the administrative region shall be adopted by the People's Congress.

Article 87 The procedures for the introduction, deliberation, and voting on bills of local regulations, autonomous regulations, and separate regulations shall, in accordance with the Organic Law of the Local People's Congresses and Local People's Governments of the People's Republic of China, and with reference to the provisions of Section 2, Section 3, and Section 5 of Chapter II of this Law, be prescribed by the People's Congress at the corresponding level.
The draft local regulation shall be reported by the organ responsible for unified deliberation, together with a report on the results of deliberation and a revised draft.

Article 88 Local regulations formulated by the People's Congress of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall be promulgated by announcement of the Presidium of the Congress.
Local regulations formulated by the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall be promulgated by announcement of the Standing Committee.
Local regulations formulated by the People's Congress or its Standing Committee of a city divided into districts or an autonomous prefecture, after being approved, shall be promulgated by announcement of the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the city divided into districts or autonomous prefecture.
Autonomous regulations and separate regulations, after being approved, shall be promulgated respectively by announcement of the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the autonomous region, autonomous prefecture, or autonomous county.

Article 89 After local regulations, autonomous regulations, and separate regulations are promulgated, their texts, as well as the explanations of the drafts and reports on the results of deliberation, shall promptly be published in the Bulletin of the Standing Committee of the People's Congress at the corresponding level, on the website of the National People's Congress (npc.gov.cn), on the local People's Congress website, and in newspapers distributed within the administrative region.
The texts of local regulations, autonomous regulations, and separate regulations published in the Bulletin of the Standing Committee shall be the standard texts.

Article 90 The Standing Committee of the People's Congress of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, and of a city divided into districts or an autonomous prefecture, shall, based on actual needs, establish grassroots legislative contact points to deeply listen to the opinions of grassroots people and relevant parties on drafts of local regulations, autonomous regulations, and separate regulations.

Article 91 The ministries and commissions of the State Council, the People's Bank of China, the National Audit Office, and other organs directly under the State Council with administrative functions, as well as institutions prescribed by law, may, in accordance with the laws and the administrative regulations, decisions, and orders of the State Council, formulate rules within the scope of their respective powers.
Matters provided for in departmental rules shall be matters concerning the implementation of laws or the administrative regulations, decisions, and orders of the State Council. Without the basis of laws or the administrative regulations, decisions, and orders of the State Council, departmental rules may not establish norms that derogate from the rights of citizens, legal persons, or other organizations, or increase their obligations, nor may they increase the powers of the department or decrease its statutory duties.

Article 92 Matters that involve the scope of powers of two or more departments of the State Council shall be submitted to the State Council for the formulation of administrative regulations, or shall be jointly formulated as rules by the relevant departments of the State Council.

Article 93 The people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, and of a city divided into districts or an autonomous prefecture, may, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and the local regulations of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, formulate rules.
Local government rules may provide for the following matters:
(1) Matters requiring the formulation of rules for the implementation of laws, administrative regulations, or local regulations;
(2) Specific administrative matters of the respective administrative region.
The formulation of local government rules by the people's government of a city divided into districts or an autonomous prefecture under paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article shall be limited to matters such as urban and rural development and management, ecological civilization construction, historical and cultural protection, and grassroots governance. Local government rules that have already been formulated and involve matters beyond the scope mentioned above shall remain in effect.
Except for the city where the people's government of a province or autonomous region is located, the city where a special economic zone is located, and the larger city already approved by the State Council, the time for the people's government of other cities divided into districts or autonomous prefectures to begin formulating rules shall be synchronized with the time for such city or autonomous prefecture to begin formulating local regulations as determined by the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the province or autonomous region.
Where local regulations should be formulated but conditions are not yet mature, due to urgent needs of administrative management, local government rules may be formulated first. If administrative measures prescribed in such rules need to continue in effect after the rules have been implemented for two full years, the matter shall be submitted to the People's Congress at the corresponding level or its Standing Committee for the formulation of local regulations.
Without the basis of laws, administrative regulations, or local regulations, local government rules may not establish norms that derogate from the rights of citizens, legal persons, or other organizations, or increase their obligations.

Article 94 The procedure for formulating departmental rules of the State Council and local government rules shall be prescribed by the State Council with reference to the provisions of Chapter III of this Law.

Article 95 Departmental rules shall be decided by a ministerial meeting or a commission meeting.
Local government rules shall be decided by a standing meeting or a plenary meeting of the government.

Article 96 Departmental rules shall be promulgated by an order signed by the head of the department.
Local government rules shall be promulgated by an order signed by the governor of the province, the chairman of the autonomous region, the mayor of the municipality, or the prefect of the autonomous prefecture.

Article 97 After being signed and promulgated, departmental rules shall be promptly published in the Bulletin of the State Council or the departmental bulletin, on the Chinese Government Legal Information website (chinalaw.gov.cn), and in newspapers distributed nationwide.
After being signed and promulgated, local government rules shall be promptly published in the bulletin of the people's government at the corresponding level, on the Chinese Government Legal Information website (chinalaw.gov.cn), and in newspapers distributed within the administrative region.
The texts of rules published in the Bulletin of the State Council or the departmental bulletin, and in the bulletin of the local people's government, shall be the standard texts.

Article 98 The Constitution has the highest legal effect. No laws, administrative regulations, local regulations, autonomous regulations and separate regulations, or rules shall contravene the Constitution.

Article 99 The legal effect of laws is higher than that of administrative regulations, local regulations, and rules.
The legal effect of administrative regulations is higher than that of local regulations and rules.

Article 100 The legal effect of local regulations is higher than that of local government rules at the corresponding level and at the lower level.
The legal effect of rules formulated by the people's governments of provinces and autonomous regions is higher than that of rules formulated by the people's governments of divided cities and autonomous prefectures within their respective administrative regions.

Autonomous regulations and separate regulations that, according to law, make adaptive provisions for laws, administrative regulations, and local regulations shall apply the provisions of the autonomous regulations and separate regulations within the autonomous region.
Regulations of special economic zones that, under authorization, make adaptive provisions for laws, administrative regulations, and local regulations shall apply the provisions of the regulations of special economic zones within the special economic zone.
Departmental rules have the same effect among themselves as between departmental rules and local government rules, and shall come into force within their respective scope of authority.

Where special provisions are inconsistent with general provisions in laws, administrative regulations, local regulations, autonomous regulations, separate regulations, or rules enacted by the same authority, the special provisions shall prevail; where new provisions are inconsistent with old provisions, the new provisions shall prevail.

Laws, administrative regulations, local regulations, autonomous regulations, separate regulations, and rules shall not be retroactive, except for special provisions made to better protect the rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations.

Where new general provisions of a law are inconsistent with old special provisions of another law on the same matter and it cannot be determined which to apply, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall rule.
Where new general provisions of an administrative regulation are inconsistent with old special provisions of another administrative regulation on the same matter and it cannot be determined which to apply, the State Council shall rule.

Where the State Council, the Central Military Commission, the National Commission of Supervision, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Standing Committees of the People's Congresses of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government consider that an administrative regulation, local regulation, autonomous regulation, or separate regulation conflicts with the Constitution or a law, or that there are issues of constitutionality or legality, they may submit a written request for review to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, and the relevant special committees of the National People's Congress and the working bodies of the Standing Committee shall conduct the review and provide opinions.
Where state organs other than those specified in the preceding paragraph, social organizations, enterprises, public institutions, and citizens consider that an administrative regulation, local regulation, autonomous regulation, or separate regulation conflicts with the Constitution or a law, they may submit a written suggestion for review to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, and the working bodies of the Standing Committee shall conduct the review; when necessary, the matter shall be referred to the relevant special committees for review and provision of opinions.

The special committees of the National People's Congress and the working bodies of the Standing Committee may conduct proactive review of administrative regulations, local regulations, autonomous regulations, separate regulations, and other normative documents submitted for archival filing, and may conduct special reviews as needed.
The archival filing review work body of the State Council may conduct proactive review of local regulations, autonomous regulations, separate regulations, departmental rules, and rules enacted by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government that are submitted for archival filing, and may conduct special reviews as needed.

Where, during the review, a special committee of the National People's Congress or a working body of the Standing Committee considers that an administrative regulation, local regulation, autonomous regulation, or separate regulation conflicts with the Constitution or a law, or that there are issues of constitutionality or legality, it may submit a written review opinion to the enacting authority; alternatively, the Constitution and Law Committee may, together with the relevant special committees and the working bodies of the Standing Committee, convene a joint review meeting, require the enacting authority to attend and provide explanations, and then submit a written review opinion to the enacting authority. The enacting authority shall, within two months, consider and provide an opinion on whether to amend or annul the regulation and provide feedback to the Constitution and Law Committee of the National People's Congress, the relevant special committee, or the working bodies of the Standing Committee.
Where the Constitution and Law Committee of the National People's Congress, the relevant special committee, or the working bodies of the Standing Committee submit a review opinion to the enacting authority in accordance with the preceding paragraph, and the enacting authority amends or annuls the administrative regulation, local regulation, autonomous regulation, or separate regulation in accordance with the opinion, the review shall be terminated.
Where, after review, the Constitution and Law Committee of the National People's Congress, the relevant special committee, or the working bodies of the Standing Committee consider that an administrative regulation, local regulation, autonomous regulation, or separate regulation conflicts with the Constitution or a law, or that there are issues of constitutionality or legality requiring amendment or annulment, but the enacting authority fails to amend or annul it, they shall submit a proposal or suggestion for annulment to the Council of Chairpersons, and the Council of Chairpersons shall decide whether to submit it to the Standing Committee for deliberation and decision.

The relevant special committees of the National People's Congress and the working bodies of the Standing Committee shall, in accordance with the prescribed requirements, provide feedback on the review results to the state organs, social organizations, enterprises, public institutions, and citizens that submitted the review suggestions, and may make the information public.

The review procedures of other authorities that accept archival filings for local regulations, autonomous regulations, separate regulations, and rules submitted for archival filing shall be prescribed by the authorities that accept such filings, in accordance with the principle of maintaining the unity of the legal system.

The archival filing review authority shall establish and improve a linkage mechanism for archival filing review, and shall promptly transfer any review request or review suggestion that should be handled by another authority to the relevant authority for processing.

The enacting authority shall conduct a review of laws, administrative regulations, local regulations, autonomous regulations, separate regulations, rules, and other regulatory documents in accordance with the principle of maintaining the unity of the legal system and the needs of reform and development.

The Central Military Commission shall, in accordance with the Constitution and laws, enact military regulations.
The various theater commands, services and arms of the People's Liberation Army of China, and the Chinese People's Armed Police Force may, in accordance with the laws and the military regulations, decisions, and orders of the Central Military Commission, formulate military rules within their respective scope of authority.
Military regulations and military rules shall be implemented within the armed forces.
The methods for formulating, amending, and abolishing military regulations and military rules shall be prescribed by the Central Military Commission in accordance with the principles provided for in this Law.

The National Commission of Supervision shall, in accordance with the Constitution, laws, and relevant decisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, formulate supervision regulations and report them to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for archival filing.

Interpretations of the specific application of laws in adjudication or procuratorial work made by the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate shall primarily address specific legal provisions and shall conform to the legislative intent, principles, and original meaning. Where a circumstance provided for in Paragraph 2 of Article 48 of this Law exists, a request for legislative interpretation or a proposal for enacting or amending relevant laws shall be submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.
Interpretations of the specific application of laws in adjudication or procuratorial work made by the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate shall be reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for archival filing within thirty days of their promulgation.
No adjudicatory or procuratorial organs other than the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate may make interpretations of the specific application of laws.
This Law shall come into force as of July 1, 2000.
